sentences.english_text: Well, his friend, Mr. Wind, would take him on another adventure.
I'm ready for some more fun, Mr. Wind!
But there was no reply.
The wind had gone and left him.
Mr. Wind!
Mr. Wind!
But there was only the echo of his voice down the empty streets.
I wish there was someone to play with.
He bounced up against the window of a little girl's bedroom.
And it was the little girl he had saved by becoming a rainbow.
Her face was a nice pink color, and she was sound asleep.
I'm glad I saved her.
It was one of my best adventures.
And he thought about his other adventures.
He thought about Leepy, the grasshopper who had saved him from the sun and had taught him to count.
Even though I'm a hailstone now, I can still count.
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
That was nice of Leepy to teach me.
I should have thanked him.
Andrippy thought about the Queen Bee, who had saved his life.
She was very nice.
I should have thanked her.
And the wind had saved him from the hummingbird.
And he had never thanked the wind.
He taught me the days of the week.
I'll bet I'm the only hailstone who knows them.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.
And there were the butterflies he had played tennis with.
And the shark that had swallowed him.
I'll bet I'm the only raindrop that ever got drunk.
And he remembered how dizzy he had been.
And how he rode on the wing of the airplane.
And he remembered the elephant and the peacock.
The peacock had been nice enough to teach him the different colors.
Andrippy said them out loud.
Green and blue and violet and black and purple.
And he thought about all the other animals in the zoo.
The snail saved me, but I didn't thank him either.
Or the owl.
The owl taught me the twelve months of the year.
He wondered if he could remember them.
He started to say them very slowly.
And then he began to recite them faster.
Janky said, He started to say them very slowly.
And then he began to recite them faster.
January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, and December.
And now the owl is dead.
I'll never see him again.
And he felt sad.
And it was a strange feeling because Drippy had never felt sad before.
He had only thought about himself and how wonderful he was.
But now, all alone in the middle of a strange city, he started to think about others.
And how nice everyone had been to him.
I should have said thank you to the owl.
But now it's too late.
And for the first time in his life, Drippy realized that you must say thank you.
While there is still time, that when people do nice things for you, you must let them know you appreciate it.
